image_description: A close-up photograph of a pale cream to light beige coral fungus (Ramaria or Clavulina species) growing on the forest floor among decaying leaves and twigs. The fungus exhibits a dense, intricate branching structure resembling marine coral, with numerous cylindrical branches arising from a central base and dividing into finer, club-shaped tips.

While the color is pale cream/beige rather than 'vivid', it falls within the natural variation of coral fungi (which can be white/cream), and the structural resemblance is perfect.
